findings.F1: Across all coins, the next day's excess return falls as the day's return grows, in units of the coin's 20-day volatility (Spearman rho −0.046 over 21,371 daily cases, t −6.7); after the 10 % weakest days the next day is +0.30 % (t 2.5) and after the 7th–9th deciles it is −0.24 % to −0.17 % (t −2.6 to −1.7), though the strongest-day decile breaks the slope at +0.16 % (t 1.2).
findings.F2: A coin's 5-day excess return rises with its rising volatility, the ratio of its 20-day to its 60-day daily volatility (rho +0.049, t 2.8, 3,188 non-overlapping cases); the top quintile of the ratio is followed by +1.11 % (t 2.5) and the bottom quintile by −0.76 % (t −1.8).
findings.F3: The same holds for the width of the day's bar, (high − low) / close: rho +0.046 (t 3.2, 4,804 cases), with +1.22 % over the next 5 days in the widest quintile (t 2.7) against −0.40 % in the narrowest. That move is about 5 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade.
findings.F4: The 5-day reversal shows only when volatility is high: among cases above the coin's median 20-day volatility, the prior 5-day return in volatility units predicts the next 5 days with rho −0.061 (t −2.8, 2,104 cases), against rho +0.014 (t 0.6) in low volatility; by year the rho is negative in every year from 2022 to 2025, down to −0.128 in 2025.
findings.F5: The tested forecast does not grade its outcome: among positive-forecast cases the quintiles run −0.11 %, +0.52 %, +0.01 %, +0.63 %, +0.72 % (rho +0.012, t 0.6, 2,489 cases); trades in the lowest entry-forecast quartile net +6.46 % against +3.40 % in the second.
findings.F6: Most of the book's gain is market exposure, not timing: positive-forecast cases beat zero-forecast cases by 0.73 % over 5 days (+0.35 % vs −0.38 %), and on the book's worst and best 2 % days the coins move −9.97 % and +8.65 % against the book's −4.11 % and +4.62 %. The Calmar shortfall comes from 2022 (book −35 % annualised mean) and 2018 (−8 %).
findings.F7: Next-day excess returns differ by weekday: Monday −0.28 % (t −3.5), Tuesday +0.29 % (t 3.2), Wednesday −0.27 % (t −3.1), Friday +0.29 % (t 4.3). These pool 15 coins that trade on the same days, so the t is overstated, and the pattern is not graded.

ideas.idea: The more a coin's 20-day volatility has risen above its 60-day volatility, and the wider its latest daily range relative to its close, the larger its rise over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long on coins whose volatility is expanding and refuse longs on coins whose volatility has gone quiet.
ideas.name: volatility expansion precedes rise

ideas.idea: When a coin's 20-day volatility is high for that coin, the lower its 5-day return measured in its own volatility, the larger its rise over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: In turbulent periods a trader would buy a coin's sharp 5-day selloffs and avoid buying its sharp 5-day run-ups.
ideas.name: high-volatility weekly reversal

ideas.idea: The more a coin's daily return falls below zero, measured in its 20-day volatility, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader would take a one-day long after a coin's unusually large down day, and refuse to chase it after a strong up day.
ideas.name: one-day reversal after drops
